verification.method: scripts/verify/health-116.py reads the original World Bank zips (data/raw/wdi/), not the site's generated data; check-wdi.mjs compares all 166,440 generated WDI values with the original files; then the text was read by hand
verification.what: every ranking row (196 countries and areas, order and value), the CSV (under-5, infant and 1990 values), every figure in the text, FAQ, title, description and JSON-LD; claims: Nigeria, Niger, Somalia highest and San Marino, Estonia, Luxembourg lowest, all top 20 in sub-Saharan Africa, world rate down 60% since 1990 and up in 2021-22, Bangladesh down 79% and below the world rate; definitions and caveats from the World Bank indicator notes
verification.against: World Bank WDI bulk files and indicator metadata (update 11 November 2026, CC BY 4.0; estimates of the UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation)
verification.result: All automated comparisons matched; caveat wording was aligned with the World Bank's notes (incomplete vital registration in developing countries) before publishing

changelog.note: First version: World Bank WDI (UN IGME) under-5 and infant mortality for 2024.
